name: Caracas Cathedral
scope: Standing Metropolitan Cathedral of Santa Ana in Caracas, with its Baroque facade, five-nave body, tower and attached chapels.
era: Standing cathedral after the 1930s and 1967 interventions. The historic Lessmann original informs the earlier standing facade and tower massing. Later fittings use written records.

originalReview.notes: The circa-1870 original viewed from Plaza Bolívar, with the original five-nave cathedral massing, stepped and articulated Baroque front, arched entry and reduced-height multi-tiered clock tower. Precise modern fittings use the written record.

review.method: Exact public-domain Lessmann original with the mapped cathedral perimeter and written inventory of later fabric
review.notes: Exact Qualla archival original by Federico Lessmann, circa 1870, resolves the stepped facade and left bell tower. Its Zeno catalogue identifier and public-domain labels match the Commons original. The primary modern report documents subsequent remodelling, five naves, the extant clock and glass. The independently mapped Museo Sacro is excluded.
